questions.text: Tariff & Bundle Clarity: Understandable pricing: (1) Clear cost per MB/min; (2) Validity period clarity (24h vs 1 day); (3) Rollover terms disclosure; (4) Out-of-bundle rate visibility; (5) Tax inclusion (VAT/Excise); (6) Promotional terms (hidden conditions?); (7) Comparison tools availability.
questions.evidence_required: Tariff sheets, USSD menu screenshots, Marketing material review
questions.africa_specific_notes: Complex bundles confuse users. 'Unlimited' often has hidden caps. Taxes (Excise) often high and hidden.

questions.text: Premium Rate Services (VAS) Transparency: Prevent unwanted charges: (1) Double opt-in for subscriptions; (2) Clear pricing for ringback tones/games; (3) Unsubscribe instructions visibility; (4) Monthly statement of VAS charges; (5) Prevention of 'clickjacking' subscriptions; (6) Refund policy for accidental subs; (7) Adult content labeling.
questions.evidence_required: VAS subscription flow logs, Opt-in confirmation messages, Complaint logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Predatory VAS is a plague. Users find credit drained by services they didn't knowingly sign up for.

questions.text: Data Usage Visibility: Real-time tracking: (1) Real-time balance check (USSD/App); (2) Detailed usage history (which app used data?); (3) Background data warnings; (4) Low balance alerts; (5) Data manager tools in-app; (6) Accuracy of metering; (7) Dispute resolution for data drain.
questions.evidence_required: App usage screens, Metering audit reports, Alert logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Users suspect Telcos of 'stealing' data. Detailed usage logs build trust. Background updates on smartphones consume expensive data.

questions.text: Fair Usage Policy (FUP) Disclosure: Throttling rules: (1) Clear definition of 'Unlimited'; (2) Throttling speed disclosure; (3) Notification when FUP hit; (4) Reset timing; (5) Policy accessibility; (6) Justification for FUP limits; (7) Business vs Consumer FUP distinction.
questions.evidence_required: FUP terms, Throttling notification SMS, Website T&Cs
questions.africa_specific_notes: 'Unlimited' usually means 1GB/day then slow speed. Users feel cheated if not clear.

questions.text: Outage Notification: Informing users of downtime: (1) Proactive SMS/Social media alerts; (2) Estimated Time to Repair (ETR) provision; (3) Reason for outage disclosure (fiber cut?); (4) Affected area map; (5) Apology/Compensation (free data?); (6) Planned maintenance warnings; (7) Post-incident report.
questions.evidence_required: Outage SMS logs, Social media posts, Incident reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Silence during outages breeds anger. Proactive communication is rare but highly valued.

questions.text: Coverage Map Accuracy: Honest coverage representation: (1) Publicly available maps; (2) Granularity (street level vs city level); (3) Distinction between 2G/3G/4G; (4) Updates for new sites; (5) Crowdsourced verification (e.g., OpenSignal); (6) Disclaimer on indoor coverage; (7) Future rollout plans.
questions.evidence_required: Public coverage map URL, Map update logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Marketing maps often exaggerate reality. Users buy SIMs only to find no signal at home.

questions.text: Privacy Policy & Data Sharing: How data is used: (1) Clear privacy policy (local language?); (2) Third-party sharing disclosure (advertisers?); (3) Government access transparency (transparency reports); (4) Data retention period; (5) User right to access/delete; (6) Call Record (CDR) privacy; (7) Mobile Money transaction privacy.
questions.evidence_required: Privacy policy, Transparency reports, Data sharing agreements
questions.africa_specific_notes: Governments often demand data without warrants. Telcos must balance license obligations with user privacy.

questions.text: SIM Registration Transparency: Handling of ID data: (1) Purpose of collection disclosure; (2) Storage security of ID copies; (3) Prevention of ID misuse (agents selling IDs); (4) Verification process transparency; (5) Deregistration process; (6) Handling of deceased users' SIMs; (7) Linking to other databases.
questions.evidence_required: SIM registration protocols, Agent training docs, Data protection audit
questions.africa_specific_notes: SIM registration mandatory everywhere. Agents often take photos of IDs on personal phones (risk).

scoring_notes: Layer 2 (Transparency) for Telecom in SSA: Billing transparency is the primary consumer demand. Privacy transparency is the primary civil society demand.
